summary: The Fire Brand storm caller is already wired to force expert fireball casting. JavaScript stops in the skilled fireball/cone-of-cold arm of spell.c:spelleffects() before the C target chooser runs. Port spell.c’s target-selection helper family and wire this arm to reach the existing explosion implementation; account for getpos highlight callback state as part of the target chooser.

source.branch: For SPE_FIREBALL or SPE_CONE_OF_COLD when role_skill is at least P_SKILLED, including Fire Brand FIRESTORM/SNOWSTORM invocation: artifact.c temporarily sets the spell-category skill to P_EXPERT and calls spelleffects(..., force=TRUE), so this arm calls throwspell() and, on acceptance, emits a randomized sequence of explosions around the chosen center.
functions: spelleffects() skilled SPE_FIREBALL/SPE_CONE_OF_COLD arm1420–1452 (bounded production caller only; no whole spelleffects credit)
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/artifact.c:2040-2050 invoke_storm_spell() raises the spell skill to P_EXPERT and calls spelleffects(storm, FALSE, TRUE); artifact.c:2169-2171 routes FIRESTORM/SNOWSTORM to it. The existing JavaScript caller mirrors this at js/artifacts.js:2588-2601 and 2709-2712.

nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:1422 calls throwspell() from the skilled fireball/cone-of-cold branch; the current JavaScript caller at js/spell.js:1403-1410 frees the pseudo object and throws UnsupportedSpellCastError instead.
dependencies: Whole getpos.c:getpos_sethilite (41–63) is absent. Existing js/getpos.js:getpos_getvalids_selection and forceGetposSelectionRedraw approximate only current-callback redraw at getpos entry. Source requires union of old/new valid locations before callback installation, persistent hilite/default state, map-frame color and changed-state redraw; getpos clears callbacks via sethilite(NULL,NULL) at getpos.c1164. Reconcile that adapter through the canonical setter and bounded getpos/apply caller wiring without claiming whole getpos or selvar completion. All active external setter callers include read.c1898 seffects_stinking_cloud and3090 cast_stinking_cloud, plus apply.c2062 jump/3464 polearm/3757 grapple. Existing JS read/apply callers use direct assignment and cleanup; reconcile those five callers and canonical getpos.c toggle/refresh/exit without new credit for broader bodies.

explode.c:explode() is implemented in js/explode.js; zap.c:spell_damage_bonus() and zapyourself() are implemented in js/zap.js. The selected spell branch still needs to wire and supply their C arguments in source order.
The self-target branch also calls attrib.c:losehp(); preserve this existing caller contract if targeting the hero is reachable.

C walk_path belongs to dothrow.c:656–735, not hack.c; reuse the existing awaited js/dothrow.js owner. The existing cansee/canspotmon/tmp_at, clearTtyMessageWindow, explode, zapyourself, spell_damage_bonus and losehp owners require direct source argument/order audit.

C caller trace: nethack-c/upstream/src/artifact.c:2040-2050 temporarily sets P_SKILL(skill)=P_EXPERT and calls spelleffects(storm,FALSE,TRUE); artifact.c:2169-2171 dispatches FIRESTORM/SNOWSTORM to invoke_storm_spell(). The matching production caller already exists at js/artifacts.js:2588-2601, 2709-2712, so artifact dispatch is not the missing owner.

C behavior trace: nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:1419-1449 enters the skilled arm, calls throwspell(), chooses rnd(8)+1 explosions, invokes explode() or zapyourself()/losehp() for self-target, and consumes rnd(3) offsets with visibility, wall, and swallowed checks that reflect invalid locations to the center. The JavaScript refusal occurs before this logic; js/explode.js and js/zap.js already contain the explosion and spell-damage helpers.

The source helper family is contiguous in nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:1607-1701: spell_aim_step() accepts zap-passable squares or open doors; can_center_spell_location() limits the center to visible, non-stone-wall squares within distance 10; display_spell_target_positions() highlights those centers; throwspell() handles water, user cancellation, range, swallowing, target visibility and walls, then walks the path and sets u.dx/u.dy. throwspell() calls getpos.c:getpos_sethilite() (41-63), so the task must preserve the callback state consumed by the existing getpos implementation.

spell_aim_step() and can_center_spell_location() are pure source helpers and need source-pinned result tests. display_spell_target_positions() and throwspell() are impure; this case’s recorded C path provides the applicable runtime evidence once it matches through the relevant steps.

Three apply.c callers install callbacks directly (polearm, grapple, jump); source setter/cycler/getpos-exit call sites must remain aligned. This is a source-backed dependency boundary, not permission to replace callbacks by test injection.
